## Purpose

This report demonstrates a three-level outcome analysis in which repeated measurements are nested within people and people are nested within organizations.

## Reproduce the workflow

~~~{r}
#| label: run-analysis
source("../R/01_generate_nested_data.R")
source("../R/02_fit_multilevel_models.R")
source("../R/03_model_diagnostics.R")
~~~

## Variance decomposition

~~~{r}
#| label: variance-components
variance <- readr::read_csv(
  "../outputs/variance_components.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(variance, digits = 3)
~~~

The unconditional model separates organization, person, and observation-level variance. This establishes whether clustering is practically important before the conditional model is interpreted.

## Fixed effects

~~~{r}
#| label: fixed-effects
fixed <- readr::read_csv(
  "../outputs/fixed_effects.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(fixed, digits = 3)
~~~

The time-by-program coefficient represents the additional average change per wave in program organizations relative to comparison organizations, conditional on the model covariates and random-effects structure.

## Diagnostic checks

Residual patterns, fitted trajectories, convergence warnings, and the distribution of organization effects are reviewed together. A production analysis would add influence diagnostics, alternative covariance structures, missing-wave analysis, and small-cluster corrections when warranted.
